core.filter.http.security.policy.title: policy
core.filter.http.security.policy.description: Embeds the Praxis Policy Engine in-process to enforce multi-source JWT identity, APL route policy, RFC 8693 token exchange, PII scanning, audit emission, and (under `body_access: read_write`) request / response body rewriting.

schema.description:
Body-access tier. `ReadOnly` (default) lets APL inspect request
and response bodies for routing / policy decisions but discards
any mutations. `ReadWrite` enables the CMF → JSON-RPC
re-serialization round-trip so APL field mutators
(e.g. `args.ssn: redact(!perm.view_ssn)`) rewrite the upstream
body and response. Pay the round-trip cost only when needed.
Filesystem path to the policy document.

Maximum time, in seconds, to wait for `PolicyEngine::initialize`
at filter construction. Identity plugins fetch JWKS over HTTPS
during init; a reachable-but-unresponsive identity provider
would otherwise hang startup or hot-reload indefinitely. On
expiry, filter construction returns an error and the server
fails fast.

30s is generous for legitimate cold-cache JWKS fetches over the
public internet, while short enough that misbehavior is noticed
during the deploy.

Maximum request/response body bytes buffered in `ReadWrite`
mode. `ReadWrite` uses `StreamBuffer` to accumulate the whole
body before APL field mutators run; without a cap an oversized
payload could exhaust memory. Ignored in `ReadOnly` mode, which
streams. The pipeline rejects an unbounded buffer at config
load, so this always carries a concrete ceiling.

Allow policy-engine calls to private or loopback identity providers.

Disabled by default to limit SSRF through policy-defined endpoints. This
does not affect Praxis upstreams, which use
`insecure_options.allow_private_endpoints`.

Fail-closed policy gate for misconfigured chains. When `true`
(default), `on_request_body` rejects any request that reaches
it without `mcp.method` filter-metadata. The metadata is set
by the protocol classifier filter (available in the `praxis-ai` package), so
its absence means either (a) the protocol classifier filter is missing from
the chain, or (b) it is ordered AFTER `policy` instead of
before. Either is a misconfiguration that would silently
bypass CMF/APL policy.

Set to `false` only when intentionally fronting non-classified
traffic through the `policy` filter for identity-only
enforcement (legacy behavior).

Only consulted when the loaded policy declares entity routes
(tool/prompt/resource). A pure-L7 (`global`-only) or identity-only
policy never reaches this gate — `on_request_body` returns
`BodyDone` before it, so the flag has no effect there.

Note: JSON-RPC methods that legitimately carry no entity (e.g.
`tools/list`, `initialize`, `prompts/list`) still pass —
`require_protocol_metadata` only rejects when the metadata is
missing entirely.

Each entry is a path with `{name}` placeholders, e.g.

labeled with the template instead of the router's path-match
pattern, keeping the label stable and bounded while staying more
precise than a prefix match.

Defaults to 140.

filters.name: access_log
filters.description: Logs structured access records for each request and response.

examples.yaml:
filter: access_log
sample_rate: 0.1   # optional; log ~10% of requests (default 1.0)
fields:            # optional; replaces default ten fields when present
  - method
  - path
  - status
  - duration_ms
  - request_header.user-agent
  - trace_id
request_headers: [user-agent]   # optional; pairs with request_header.* tokens
response_headers: [content-type]
conditions:                   # optional emit-time gates (AND across keys)
  min_duration_ms: 1000
  status_classes: [4xx, 5xx]  # OR within list
  paths: ["/api"]             # OR within list; segment-boundary prefixes

filters.name: request_id
filters.description: Ensures every request carries a correlation ID.

examples.yaml:
filter: request_id
header_name: X-Correlation-ID   # optional

filters.name: trace_context
filters.description: Propagates W3C Trace Context headers (`traceparent`, `tracestate`).

examples.yaml: filter: trace_context

filters.name: compression
filters.description: Enables Pingora's built-in response compression when present in a filter chain.

examples.yaml:
filter: compression
level: 6                        # default level for all algorithms
min_size_bytes: 256             # skip responses smaller than this
gzip:
  enabled: true
  level: 6
brotli:
  enabled: true
  level: 4
zstd:
  enabled: true
  level: 3
content_types:
  - "text/"
  - "application/json"
  - "application/javascript"
  - "application/xml"
  - "application/wasm"

filters.name: json_body_field
filters.description: Extracts top-level fields from a JSON request body and promotes their values to request headers using [`StreamBuffer`] mode.

examples.yaml:
filter: json_body_field
field: model
header: X-Model

filter: json_body_field
fields:
  - field: model
    header: X-Model
  - field: user_id
    header: X-User-Id

filters.name: json_rpc
filters.description: Extracts JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope metadata from request bodies and promotes method, id, and kind to request headers and filter results for routing.

examples.yaml: filter: json_rpc

filter: json_rpc
max_body_bytes: 1048576
batch_policy: first
max_batch_size: 50
on_invalid: continue
headers:
  method: X-Json-Rpc-Method
  id: X-Json-Rpc-Id
  kind: X-Json-Rpc-Kind

filters.name: basic_auth
filters.description: HTTP Basic Authentication filter (RFC 7617).

examples.yaml:
filter: basic_auth
realm: "Restricted"
strip_authorization: true
credentials:
  - username: admin
    password: secret
  - username: deploy
    env_var: DEPLOY_PASSWORD

filters.name: cors
filters.description: Spec-compliant CORS filter implementing origin validation, preflight handling, and response header injection.

examples.yaml:
filter: cors
allow_origins:
  - "https://app.example.com"
  - "https://*.example.com"
allow_methods:
  - GET
  - POST
  - PUT
allow_headers:
  - Content-Type
  - Authorization
expose_headers:
  - X-Request-ID
max_age: 3600
allow_credentials: false

filters.name: credential_injection
filters.description: Injects per-cluster API credentials into upstream requests.

examples.yaml:
filter: credential_injection
clusters:
  - name: provider-a
    header: Authorization
    env_var: PROVIDER_A_API_KEY
    header_prefix: "Bearer "
    strip_client_credential: true
  - name: internal
    header: x-api-key
    value: "internal-secret"

filters.name: csrf
filters.description: CSRF protection filter that validates request origins against a trusted allowlist.

examples.yaml:
filter: csrf
trusted_origins:
  - "https://app.example.com"
  - "https://*.example.com"
enforce_percentage: 100
enable_sec_fetch_site: true

filters.name: forwarded_headers
filters.description: Injects `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, and `X-Forwarded-Host` headers into upstream requests.

examples.yaml:
filter: forwarded_headers
trusted_proxies: ["10.0.0.0/8"]
use_standard_header: true

filters.name: guardrails
filters.description: Rejects requests matching string, regex, or PII rules against headers and/or body content.

examples.yaml:
filter: guardrails
action: flag            # or "reject" (default)
rules:
  # Detect PII in a header
  - target: header
    name: "Authorization"
    contains: [ssn, credit_card, email]
  # Detect PII in body
  - target: body
    contains: [ssn, credit_card, phone, email]
  # Block SQL injection in body
  - target: body
    contains: "DROP TABLE"
  # Block requests from bad bots
  - target: header
    name: "User-Agent"
    pattern: "bad-bot.*"
  # Require body to look like JSON (reject if NOT matching)
  - target: body
    pattern: "^\\{.*\\}$"
    negate: true

filters.name: ip_acl
filters.description: IP-based access control filter.

filters.name: peer_identity_trust
filters.description: Validates that the downstream mTLS peer identity matches a configured trusted peer before allowing the request to continue.

examples.yaml:
filter: peer_identity_trust
trusted_peers:
  - cert_digest: "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa"
  - cert_digest: "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb"
    organization: example-org

filters.name: policy
filters.description: Embeds the Praxis Policy Engine in-process to enforce multi-source JWT identity, APL route policy, RFC 8693 token exchange, PII scanning, audit emission, and (under `body_access: read_write`) request / response body rewriting.

examples.yaml:
filter: policy
config_path: /etc/praxis/policy.yaml
body_access: read_write       # optional; default read_only
require_protocol_metadata: true    # optional; default true
init_timeout_secs: 30         # optional; default 30
max_buffer_bytes: 10485760    # optional; default 10 MiB (read_write only)

filters.name: circuit_breaker
filters.description: Rejects requests to clusters whose circuit is open.

examples.yaml:
filter: circuit_breaker
clusters:
  - name: backend
    consecutive_failures: 5
    recovery_window_secs: 30

filters.name: endpoint_selector
filters.description: Selects an upstream endpoint from a trusted mutation source.

examples.yaml:
filter: endpoint_selector
source_header: x-gateway-destination-endpoint
strip_header: true  # default true
connection:
  connection_timeout_ms: 1000
  total_connection_timeout_ms: 2000
tls:
  sni: inference.example.internal

filters.name: grpc_detection
filters.description: Detects gRPC requests from the `content-type` header and promotes the variant to filter metadata and results for downstream routing.

examples.yaml: filter: grpc_detection

filters.name: iterative_request_router
filters.description: Framework-level filter for iterative sub-request execution.

examples.yaml:
filter: iterative_request_router
initial_step: model-call
steps:
  - name: model-call
    filters:
      - filter: router
        routes:
          - cluster: llm-backend
      - filter: load_balancer
        clusters:
          - name: llm-backend
            endpoints: ["10.0.0.1:8000"]
    on_result:
      - default: true
        done: true

filters.name: load_balancer
filters.description: Selects an upstream endpoint using the cluster's configured strategy.

examples.yaml:
filter: load_balancer
clusters:
  - name: backend
    endpoints: ["10.0.0.1:80"]

filters.name: rate_limit
filters.description: Token bucket rate limiter that rejects excess traffic with 429.

examples.yaml:
filter: rate_limit
mode: per_ip        # "per_ip" or "global"
rate: 100           # tokens per second
burst: 200          # max bucket capacity

filters.name: redirect
filters.description: Returns a redirect response without contacting any upstream.

examples.yaml:
filter: redirect
status: 301
location: "https://example.com${path}${query}"

filters.name: router
filters.description: Routes requests to clusters based on path prefix and host header.

examples.yaml:
filter: router
routes:
  - path_prefix: "/"
    cluster: default

filters.name: static_response
filters.description: Returns a fixed response without contacting any upstream.

examples.yaml:
filter: static_response
status: 200
body: "OK"

filters.name: sticky_sessions
filters.description: Sticky sessions HTTP filter.

examples.yaml:
filter: sticky_sessions
clusters:
  - name: app_backend
    type: cookie
    cookie_name: "_praxis_route"
    ttl_secs: 3600
    cookie_attributes:
      path: "/"
      http_only: true
      secure: true
      same_site: Lax
    failover: true
    max_entries: 100000
    eviction: lru

filters.name: timeout
filters.description: Enforces a maximum end-to-end latency from request receipt to response headers.

examples.yaml:
filter: timeout
timeout_ms: 5000   # 5 seconds

filters.name: headers
filters.description: Adds, sets, or removes headers on upstream requests and downstream responses.

examples.yaml:
filter: headers
request_add:
  - name: X-Forwarded-By
    value: praxis
request_set:
  - name: X-Custom-Auth
    value: bearer-token
request_remove:
  - X-Internal-Only
response_add:
  - name: X-Frame-Options
    value: DENY
response_remove:
  - X-Backend-Server
response_set:
  - name: Server
    value: praxis

filters.name: path_rewrite
filters.description: Rewrites the request path before forwarding to the upstream.

examples.yaml:
filter: path_rewrite
strip_prefix: "/api/v1"

filters.name: url_rewrite
filters.description: Rewrites request URLs using regex substitution and query parameter manipulation before the request reaches upstream.

examples.yaml:
filter: url_rewrite
operations:
  - regex_replace:
      pattern: "^/api/v1/(.*)"
      replacement: "/api/v2/$1"
  - strip_query_params:
      - debug
  - add_query_params:
      source: gateway

filters.name: tcp_access_log
filters.description: Logs TCP connection events.

examples.yaml:
filter: tcp_access_log
# no configurable parameters

filters.name: sni_router
filters.description: Routes TCP connections by SNI hostname.

examples.yaml:
filter: sni_router
routes:
  - server_names: ["api.example.com"]
    upstream: "10.0.0.1:443"
  - server_names: ["*.example.com"]
    upstream: "10.0.0.2:443"
default_upstream: "10.0.0.3:443"

filters.name: tcp_load_balancer
filters.description: Selects an upstream TCP endpoint using the cluster's configured strategy.

examples.yaml:
filter: tcp_load_balancer
clusters:
  - name: db_pool
    endpoints: ["10.0.0.1:5432", "10.0.0.2:5432"]
